compiled_state.title: Static-analysis defense layer for hermeticity, antipatterns, and config drift
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
EPIC_CLASS: class:architectural

## Context

DSO's pre-commit stack is entirely syntactic (paths, schemas, ticket IDs, executable bits) and has no gate for four recurring failure classes that account for roughly 40% of recent fixes:

1. $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT referenced unbound under `set -u` — an identical-root-cause chain across fe45-0b58, 09d8-11f0, 82ad-7bb3, and 97a7-4504 spanning months.
2. `echo … | grep -q` under `set -o pipefail` causing SIGPIPE on Linux — about 63 files are in violation today, up from 42 when this epic was filed; the count grows while the antipattern is uncovered.
3. `declare -A` in scripts that must run on bash 3.2, the macOS default — about 24 files.
4. Config keys added to dso-config.conf without a paired entry in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md (a190-d780).

These escape pre-commit and are only caught post-merge by the release gate (validate.sh --ci), so they recur in new files weeks apart. This epic adds the missing static-detection layer so each class is blocked at commit time, with a shrink-only baseline so the existing backlog does not block rollout.

## Success Criteria

1. Committing staged content that introduces any of the four antipattern classes is blocked locally by a dedicated hook (check-hermeticity.sh, check-known-antipatterns.sh, check-config-key-docs.sh, check-pipefail-grep.sh), all registered in .pre-commit-config.yaml between shellcheck and pre-commit-review-gate; check-pipefail-grep detects both bare-pipeline and command-substitution/subshell forms of `… | grep -q` under pipefail.
2. Each hook reads a per-hook baseline capturing the violations present when the hook ships; baselined violations do not block commits. The baseline is shrink-only and count-based: a commit is rejected if the post-commit violation count for any hook exceeds that hook's recorded baseline, and removing a baseline entry without removing the corresponding source violation is itself a rejected grow operation.
3. Each hook emits per-file diagnostics naming the offending line, the exact remediation string, and a citation to the originating ticket (e.g., e241-41b2 for SIGPIPE, a190-d780 for config-doc drift).
4. plugins/dso/config/known-antipatterns.yaml ships as an append-only registry with a documented, versioned schema (id, pattern, target languages/dirs, remediation, citation), consumed by check-known-antipatterns.sh and documented in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md. The append-only contract is mechanically guarded: a commit that removes or mutates an existing registry entry is rejected.
5. Suppression follows existing-hook precedent (# antipattern-ok: <reason>, # bash4-only:); each suppression requires a non-empty, non-whitespace justification token on the same line, and a suppression with an empty or whitespace-only reason is itself rejected.
6. Each hook ships a fixture-based test asserting (a) the antipattern is detected on staged content, (b) baselined violations do not fire, (c) new instances are blocked, and (d) baseline growth is rejected; plus (e) an end-to-end test that invokes the hook through the real pre-commit framework (covering the symlink-chain BASH_SOURCE class, ref a40e-ab52), confirming the hooks and static-defense-lib.sh resolve their own paths and baselines without CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT and pass their own checks (dogfood).
7. Staged-file enumeration in static-defense-lib.sh covers added, copied, modified, and renamed/mode-changed .sh files, so a violation introduced via a rename or mode-change is detected and not silently skipped by a restrictive --diff-filter.
8. static-defense-lib.sh and the four hooks execute correctly under bash 3.2 (the macOS default), verified by a bash-3.2-constrained test, so the shared library cannot itself ship the bash-4-only antipattern (declare -A, namerefs) that check-known-antipatterns.sh is meant to flag.

## Closure Checks

None — all success criteria are verifiable within the implementing sprint session.

## Dependencies

- Blocks 99f1-153c (fix-bug recurrence prevention): this epic creates the known-antipatterns registry that 99f1-153c populates (the A then E sequence).
- Coexists with cf7b-86a9 (shellcheck/ruff parity) — a different antipattern layer. This epic owns the hermeticity, SIGPIPE-under-pipefail, declare -A, and config-key-docs antipattern classes; cross-file bloat detectors (P-D1/P-T2/P-C2) are owned by bc7f-1a0d. The .pre-commit-config.yaml ordering comment doubles as the scope boundary.
- Reviewer-rubric counterparts (New Epic B) and registry population over time (New Epic E / 99f1-153c) are out of scope.
- Release note: if CI runs `pre-commit run --all-files`, the four hooks become active CI gates — verify CI wiring before relying on them in CI. No scripts/release.sh code change is required.

## Approach

Four pre-commit hooks share one library, plugins/dso/hooks/lib/static-defense-lib.sh, which owns rename-inclusive staged-.sh enumeration, count-based shrink-only baseline load/diff, suppression-annotation parsing, and diagnostic formatting (remediation string plus originating-ticket citation). Each hook is a thin wrapper supplying only its detection logic and message strings. check-known-antipatterns.sh reads regex/AST queries from the append-only known-antipatterns.yaml, parsed by a single pinned parser (no new dependency — yq and python3 are already available; the parser choice must not depend on yq v3-vs-v4 syntax differences). The hooks register as discrete, independently-named entries between shellcheck and pre-commit-review-gate so concurrent hook-adding epics merge without conflict. Design constraint (the highest-risk failure mode): the hooks and the shared library must themselves pass all four checks (dogfood) and must resolve their own paths and baseline locations via the BASH_SOURCE -> readlink -f idiom (the pattern already used by check-tickets-boundary.sh), never via CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, so they work correctly under the pre-commit framework's symlinked temp-path chain and in CI where CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is unset.

## Cross-Epic Interactions

- Resource: plugins/dso/config/known-antipatterns.yaml. Downstream consumers are 99f1-153c (fix-bug recurrence prevention; populates the registry), d63f-2c74 (reads registry.antipattern_path), and a47f-b451 (reviewer-rubric / bug-classification-registry alignment). Gate: this epic publishes the registry with a stable, documented, versioned schema and ships it before those consumers run; consumers must tolerate the not-yet-populated (empty registry) case.
- Resource: .pre-commit-config.yaml hook registration and ordering. Concurrent hook-adding epics are 230a-344a, bc7f-1a0d, af26-dd5a, c337-ed61, and 857d-a35a. Gate: the four hooks register as discrete, independently-named entries in the shellcheck-to-pre-commit-review-gate band so concurrent epics merge without conflict; the ordering invariant (after shellcheck, before pre-commit-review-gate) is documented in a .pre-commit-config.yaml comment.

## State Lifecycle

| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |
|----------|--------|--------|---------|--------|
| plugins/dso/config/known-antipatterns.yaml | this epic | fix-bug workflow (99f1-153c / New Epic E) plus maintainers, append-only | check-known-antipatterns.sh; downstream consumers d63f-2c74 (registry.antipattern_path) and 99f1-153c | never retired — persists for project lifetime |
| per-hook baseline files (e.g., check-pipefail-grep.baseline) | this epic (initial violation capture) | developers during remediation (shrink-only; the hook rejects growth) | the owning hook (each reads only its own baseline) | never retired — remains, possibly empty, as the ratchet floor |
| .pre-commit-config.yaml (4 new hook entries) | this epic | maintainers | pre-commit framework (local) plus CI if it runs `pre-commit run --all-files` | never retired |

## Scenario Analysis

- check-pipefail-grep subshell/command-substitution false-negative (high) — addressed by SC1.
- Shrink-only baseline merge race across worktrees (high) — addressed by SC2 count-based recompute and a documented merge strategy.
- Diff-vs-full-file scan false negative/positive (high) — addressed in the Approach (scan staged content, compare against the baseline rather than re-firing on baselined lines).
- YAML parser version divergence, yq v3 vs v4 (high) — addressed in the Approach (single pinned parser).
- Whitespace-only suppression token bypass (medium) — addressed by SC5.
- Append-only invariant not machine-enforced (medium) — addressed by SC4 mechanical guard.
- Baseline format ambiguity, integer vs file-keyed map (medium) — addressed in the Approach (one consistent format owned by the shared library).
- Rename/mode-change enumeration gap (assumption, medium) — addressed by SC7.
- static-defense-lib.sh bash-3.2 self-compatibility (assumption, high) — addressed by SC8.

## References

- docs/observed-failure-patterns-4-26.md Patterns 1, 3, 4, 7
- docs/process-gaps-4-26.md G1, G6, G11, G12
- docs/proposed-mitigations-4-26.md G1-M1, G6-M2, G11-M1, G12-M1
